chapter: Chicago: Henderson, Tatum and Roy Eldridge, then New York and the army
title: Forming and playing in Roy Eldridge's band at the Three Deuces
summary: After Eldridge left Henderson he formed a small band in Chicago with Collins, Dave Young, Scoops Carey, Zutty Singleton and Truck Parham, staying about three years.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: But any way, I -- after Art left, Roy left Fletchers.
Roy was at the Grand Terrace with Fletcher Henderson, he and Chu Berry. So Roy formed this band that I was in Roy's band.

Gosh, I can't tell you, I stayed there for three years with Roy, I imagine. And that was a tremendous band. No, we had about six -- let's see, four rhythm, and three horns. Roy Eldridge, Dave Young playing tenor, and Scoops Carey playing alto saxophone. Tremendous alto saxophone player.
We stayed here at the Three Deuces, oh, for about three years.

Old Zut. And Cozy Cole's brother, Ted Cole, and Truck Parham, the bass player, tremendous bass player. And very good band. And all the musicians, anybody who was anybody would come to the Three Deuces. That all the travelling bands when they came to town, they would -- all the travelling white bands. No black was allowed in the joint at this time. Well, it was very prejudiced -- Chicago was a very prejudiced town, you know. So --
